facts.value: The most prestigious award in mathematics, established by John Charles Fields in 1936 and awarded every four years to up to four individuals.
Instituted in 2002 and first awarded in 2003.
For lifetime achievement, introduced in 2009 and first awarded in 2010.
Awarded by the American Mathematical Society since 1970.
Also for lifetime achievement, instituted in 1978.
A famous list of 23 open problems compiled in 1900 by German mathematician David Hilbert, with at least thirteen of the problems solved.
A new list of seven important problems published in 2000, with a reward of 1 million dollars for a solution to any of these problems.
One of the Millennium Prize Problems that duplicates one of Hilbert's problems.
The only Millennium Prize Problem that has been solved, solved by Russian mathematician Grigori Perelman.
